quarterly_data.quarter: Huafeng Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual collective (05-28-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: General manager Liu Taiguo (2025 annual collective results briefing): Q1 2026 revenue was RMB 6.33 hundred million, up 56.15% year on year, and net profit attributable to shareholders RMB 1.05 hundred million, up 230.43%, continuing high growth. He attributed the growth to data-center infrastructure upgrades, the AI-compute demand boom and rising new-energy-vehicle penetration; a better product mix, with high value-added assemblies revenue up over 300% in 2025; and orderly delivery of key defense projects. He said orders on hand are sufficient and downstream demand is stable.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue RMB 6.33 hundred million (+56.15%); net profit attributable RMB 1.05 hundred million (+230.43%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Huafeng Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual collective (05-28-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Board secretary Jiang Daocai (2025 annual collective results briefing): the company says it was the first in China to break the overseas technology monopoly and develop and mass-produce high-speed cable modules, a product with high technical barriers; it built a volume-production line in 2024 and keeps upgrading it. It has deep cooperation with mainstream AI server makers Huawei, ZTE, Inspur and xFusion while advancing projects with leading internet companies; it has mastered 112Gbps high-speed transmission and is working on 224G products. General manager Liu Taiguo said R&D focuses on 224Gbps high-speed backplane connectors, high-speed cable modules and CPU Socket connectors for AI clusters, with some projects in customer validation and small-batch trial production.
quarterly_data.figure: 112Gbps mastered; 224Gbps backplane connectors, cable modules and CPU Socket connectors in customer validation / small-batch trial production

quarterly_data.quarter: Huafeng Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual collective (05-28-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: General manager Liu Taiguo (2025 annual collective results briefing): in low-altitude economy, deep-sea exploration and commercial space the company has finalised several products - its EWIS electrical wiring interconnect systems and equipment racks were delivered for low-altitude and military manned aircraft and completed first flight; it developed 56G high-speed cable assemblies for satellites and led the drafting of two commercial-space high-speed connector group standards, and will develop high-reliability high-speed connectors for commercial satellites. In new-energy vehicles its high-speed and high-voltage connectors are in the supply chains of SAIC-GM-Wuling, BYD and FAW Bestune at scale, and its vehicle optoelectronic connectors are used in several smart-driving domain controllers.
